Team —

BlueHarbor wants a clear responsibility matrix and a short SLA clause for cross-region failover. Questions we should answer in the mapping:

1) Failover activation: who performs DNS cutover vs. Redwood automatic router-level fallback? (we need the definitive owner and whether we will accept DNS control transfer or will do a coordinated cutover)
2) RPO guarantees: can we commit to cross-region async replication windows (15m/1h/NA)? Differences for Dedicated vs Hosted.
3) RTO targets: activation vs. full warm-standby readiness. Example: activation within 15m, full readiness within 60m.
4) Data responsibilities: is replication part of Dedicated offering or an optional add-on? Any constraints on retention and snapshot frequency.
5) Runbook and testing cadence: who schedules and runs DR tests; can we include annual test window in the contract?

Karthik — can you draft a proposed matrix (one-line ownership entries) and suggested numeric RTO/RPO buckets for Dedicated and Hosted? Stephanie — any compliance wording or caveats to include? Marissa — please draft procurement-friendly clause and next steps (DocuSign addendum recommendation).

Thanks — need first draft by EOD tomorrow if possible.

Kim

On Wed, Dec 5, 2028 at 11:10 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Team —
> BlueHarbor wants a clear responsibility matrix...

Draft technical mapping (short):

- DNS failover: Customer-owned (BlueHarbor). We can support an automated failover API but require delegated DNS records or automated RRSets on their DNS provider. (Owner: Customer)
- Router-level fallback (Redwood): Redwood will route traffic to healthy regions if a regional pool is marked unavailable at the edge. (Owner: Redwood)
- Data replication (Dedicated): Redwood-managed async cross-region replication available as an opt-in for Dedicated pools. Target RPO: 15 minutes with 99.9% replication success over normal load. (Owner: Redwood)
- Data replication (Hosted): Not included by default. Recommend customer manage replication or use dedicated offering. Our hosted offering provides best-effort snapshot backups with up to 24h RPO. (Owner: Customer / best-effort Redwood)
- Cache warming / prefetch: Customer-triggered during maintenance; Redwood can provide hooks and API for cache pre-warming. (Owner: Customer + Redwood tooling)
- Runbook activation: Single point of activation is via Redwood operational runbook which Redwood executes for runtime steps; DNS cutover remains customer action unless contract transfers DNS delegation. (Owner: Redwood runtime steps + Customer DNS)
- Testing cadence: Recommend annual joint DR test for contractual SLA; agreed windows and playbooks should be in addendum.

Suggested numeric commitment (proposal):
- Dedicated: RTO (activation to traffic redirection) <= 30 minutes; Full readiness (all systems warmed) <= 60 minutes; RPO <= 15 minutes.
- Hosted: RTO best-effort <= 3 hours; RPO <= 24 hours.

I'll put this into a compact matrix for procurement. Note: any hard RTO/RPO targets for Hosted will need explicit capacity reservations or Dedicated.

Karthik

Alex,

Thanks for the patience. Attached is a concise Shared Responsibility Map and a short procurement-ready SLA addendum (see runbook and annotated items). Summary below (short):

- Ownership:
  - Redwood: runtime failover routing, Dedicated cross-region async replication (if opted-in), operational runbook activation for runtime steps, telemetry and post-incident RCA.
  - Customer (BlueHarbor): authoritative DNS and DNS cutover, client-side retry policies, scheduling and approval of DR tests.

- Numeric commitments (proposed):
  - Dedicated pools (opt-in): RTO (activation) <= 30 minutes; Full warm-standby <= 60 minutes; RPO <= 15 minutes.
  - Hosted (standard): RTO best-effort <= 3 hours; RPO <= 24 hours.

- Caveats & operational notes:
  - Hard RTOs for Hosted require reserved capacity or Dedicated pools.
  - Replication SLA applies only when Redwood cross-region replication is enabled on Dedicated pools.
  - Annual joint DR test windows should be scheduled and documented in the addendum.

Suggested procurement clause (one paragraph):
"Redwood and Customer agree to a Shared Responsibility Model for cross-region failover. Redwood will be responsible for runtime routing, automated region fallback, and (when enabled for Dedicated pools) cross-region asynchronous replication with a target RPO of 15 minutes and RTO activation target of 30 minutes. The Customer will retain authoritative DNS control and is responsible for DNS cutover unless DNS delegation to Redwood is explicitly granted in this agreement. Hosted offerings are provided on a best-effort basis and are not covered by the Dedicated replication commitments. Annual joint DR testing windows will be scheduled and documented in the operational addendum."

Next steps: If the above aligns, Marissa will circulate a short addendum (DocuSign) with the map and runbook links. Marissa — can you schedule a 30-minute alignment call to finalize wording and confirm DNS delegation decision?

Regards,

Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
